structural_changes.reason: Marked the opening body row as indented: the scan aligns it with the continuation rows below, not with the flush-left headwords. Text, ID, zone and crop are unchanged.

uncertainties: c1-l016: Icuſa is the chosen reading. The long-s shoulder is damaged and partly detached above the following a; the surviving traces and the warfare gloss support ſ plus unmarked a rather than draft Iculã.

structural_changes.reason: Restored the actually typeset running header A ANTES DO V., replacing draft G ANTES DO V. A pale handwritten G to its left appears to correct the printed A and is recorded in a non-transcribed copy note rather than substituted into the typeset text.
Restored the visible full stop after the page number, 123., in the existing far-right header segment. Header placement and ID are unchanged.

Expanded the left-column crop windows from x=260, width=1110 to x=210, width=1160, keeping their right edge and all y/height values. This includes initial letters clipped by the original windows, especially lower in the slanting column, and restores outer-rule context. Every revised crop was rendered and inspected; no body row was added, removed, moved or resegmented.

uncertainties: c1-l030: enrejeiados is the chosen reading, with one r after n and no t. The unusual printed form is interpreted in the cold-of-hell context and retained without lexical normalization.
c1-l041: voitari is preferred to draft vuitari. The o is open at the abraded top; the surviving rounded shape and the old-man gloss support the chosen reading.

c1-l046: curumazani nauoru and Mudarſe are incorporated. The initial n of nauoru and parts of Mudarſe are worn; surviving strokes and the circle-positioning gloss support these choices over the draft readings.
c2-l010: vodoxitatçuru is preferred to draft vedoxitatçuru. The second vowel is worn and open; it is read as o from its remnant and the parallel armour-lacing expression.
c2-l021: The citation is retained as Tait., with a t-shaped final letter; it has not been silently regularized to Taif. or expanded to a book title.

c2-l033: The chosen text is Guxet. Vorocani toqu. Fraticar, ou pre-. The damaged o of toqu and the worn Portuguese word are the main caveats. Fraticar has an F-like initial and is retained as an apparent printing anomaly for praticar rather than corrected by expectation.

c2-l035 and c2-l037: Faſuno is read with a worn long-s shoulder, consistent with the lotus-root context and the clearer occurrence on f248. At c2-l035 the short stem and faint dot of i, replace the draft l,; these small traces remain nonblocking caveats.

structural_changes.reason: Corrected the catchword from Gǔyô. to Gǔyǒ.: enlargement shows a caron, not a circumflex, over the final o. The separate far-right catchword placement and ID are unchanged.
